editorial.headline: Railway Signalling and Telecoms: The National–Bali Position
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the systems that communicate and signal along Indonesia’s railways, with PMA open nationally and not blocked by Bali’s island-wide moratorium.
editorial.body:
Railway signalling and telecommunications installation is the work of putting in place, maintaining and repairing the systems that allow a railway to signal and communicate. That includes electrical signals installed along the track, as well as the associated railway telecommunications systems. It is an infrastructure activity with a distinctly operational remit: installation is only part of the picture; maintenance and repair belong to the same stated scope.

Nationally, the activity is **open to PMA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%**. It is available at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. For a foreign-owned business, that makes the national position unusually direct in the record: the activity is open, and the stated ownership ceiling does not require a reduced foreign stake.

Bali needs to be read on its own terms. The province permanently blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities across the island. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The record identifies the OSS risk at the Besar scale as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—which places it outside the risk categories covered by the provincial block.

That distinction matters because a national PMA opening does not, by itself, settle the Bali position. Here, however, the two layers do not conflict: the activity is open to PMA nationally at up to 100% foreign ownership, and Bali’s moratorium does not block it. The practical reading is therefore neither a blanket Bali exclusion nor an invented local condition, but a clear higher-risk position outside the moratorium’s Low and Medium-Low scope.
editorial.pullQuote: The activity is open to PMA nationally at up to 100% foreign ownership, and Bali’s moratorium does not block it.
